_comment: Expected TDX image measurements for the OS images the 0G-PC gateway is deployed
on. `pcverify -gateway` embeds this file, so nobody running it has to supply or
even know these values.
WHAT IT IS FOR. The quote's mr_config_id commits to a compose hash, but the host
chooses that register — what makes it truthful is the guest OS refusing to boot
when it disagrees with the app-compose actually delivered (dstack
config_id_verifier.rs). Trusting that check means trusting the OS doing it.
Without an entry here, a host that booted a MODIFIED dstack OS with that check
removed could commit to a published release's compose hash while running
something else, and verification would still pass.
ONE ENTRY PER IMAGE. The three registers below identify the image and nothing
else: MRTD is the virtual firmware, RTMR1 the kernel, RTMR2 the kernel cmdline
(which carries the rootfs dm-verity hash) plus the initrd. Together they measure
every piece of code that performs the boot-time check above, which is the whole
claim. RTMR0 is deliberately NOT here: it records the VM shape — vCPU count,
memory size, ACPI/device layout — which is not something this check needs to
establish, and including it would have meant an entry per (image, VM shape) pair
instead of per image. Measured, not assumed: computing the same image at 1/2G,
2/4G and 4/8G gives three different RTMR0 values and identical MRTD/RTMR1/RTMR2.
The security-relevant shape settings are covered anyway — disabling root verity
changes the cmdline and therefore RTMR2. pcverify prints RTMR0 as information so
a shape change is still visible.
ONE CAVEAT ON MRTD. It also depends on how the VMM adds pages during TD build
(dstack's `two_pass_add_pages`, i.e. vm_config.qemu_single_pass_add_pages =
false). That is a property of the host's QEMU rather than of the deployment, and
it is constant for a platform, but it means MRTD is (image, page-add mode). The
mode each entry was computed for is recorded below.
AND MRTD DOES NOT IDENTIFY AN IMAGE BY ITSELF. It measures the virtual firmware,
so two releases that ship the same ovmf.fd have the same MRTD — dstack-0.5.9 and
dstack-nvidia-0.5.4.1 below carry an identical one, and their ovmf.fd files are
byte-identical. RTMR1 (kernel) and RTMR2 (cmdline + initrd) are what separate
them, which is why a match is on all three together and never on MRTD alone.
HOW TO DERIVE ONE. Do not copy values out of a running deployment: that only
records what it currently reports, which is the thing being verified. Compute them
from the published image, then confirm they match a live quote — the computation is
independent of the deployment, and the agreement is what makes the entry mean
something.
1. Read the CVM's image name and os_image_hash (dstack vm_config;
os_image_hash IS the release's digest.txt, i.e. sha256(sha256sum.txt)).
2. Fetch that guest-OS release. WHERE depends on flavour and version:
base / dev, < 0.6.0       github.com/Dstack-TEE/meta-dstack releases
nvidia,      >= v0.5.6    github.com/Dstack-TEE/meta-dstack releases
nvidia,      <  v0.5.6    github.com/nearai/private-ml-sdk  releases
any,         >= 0.6.0     github.com/Dstack-TEE/dstack  guest-os-* releases
(the split is what Phala's own verifier uses — trust-center
packages/verifier/src/utils/imageDownloader.ts getNvidiaRepo)
3. Check the artifact, and that it is the deployment's:
sha256sum -c sha256sum.txt
test "$(sha256sum sha256sum.txt | awk '{print $1}')" = "$(cat digest.txt)"
digest.txt must equal the os_image_hash from step 1 — that, not the version
string, is what ties the artifact to the deployment.
4. Compute MRTD/RTMR1/RTMR2. Use dstack-mr's
tdx::tdx_measurements_for_image_dir_without_rtmr0(image_dir, vm_config),
which needs no QEMU: the `measure` subcommand computes RTMR0 too and so
shells out to dstack-acpi-tables. Note the Go dstack-mr
(github.com/kvinwang/dstack-mr) models no page-add mode and returns the
single-pass MRTD, which will NOT match a two-pass host.
5. Confirm all three equal what a live quote reports (`pcverify -gateway` prints
them). Only then is the entry meaningful.
6. Stronger, and worth doing once in CI: rebuild from source with the release's
reproduce.sh and confirm digest.txt matches, which removes the published
tarball from the trust path.
ADDING AN IMAGE IS NOT OPTIONAL ONCE THIS LIST IS NON-EMPTY. An unlisted image is
a FAILED check, not an unpinned one. So deploying on a new OS image version needs
an entry here first — per image version, not per deployment or per replica.
An empty `images` list means NOT CONFIGURED: pcverify reports the OS image as
unpinned and says so in its summary, rather than failing. It never means
'accept anything' — see attest.BootChainPolicy.
Fields: `name`, `os_image_hash`, `source` and `page_add` are provenance — which
release this entry was computed from and how — and are never matched on. `mrtd`,
`rtmr1`, `rtmr2` are hex, 48 bytes each, and are the value compared.

images.name: dstack-0.5.9
note: Computed from the published artifact with dstack-mr (dstack e2d70a3),
2/4G, 4/8G and 16/32G. STEP 5 IS STILL OPEN: these have not yet been
confirmed against a live quote, because no CVM runs this image yet. The
same command on the same tool reproduces all three of the entry above,
which a live quote HAS confirmed — that is what this entry rests on until
the first deployment on 0.5.9 either agrees or does not. A wrong value here
can only reject that deployment, never accept a foreign one.
